checks.title: Robot checks
checks.none: Run the checks to see results.

RB-C-01.title: Climb
RB-C-01.asks: Can the drive train move the robot on this slope?
RB-C-01.note: Wheel torque available against torque needed, with iynk's margin of 1.5.

RB-C-02.title: Top speed
RB-C-02.asks: How fast can the robot go with this motor, gear and supply?
RB-C-02.note: Wheel radius times speed with no load over the gear ratio, at the supply minus the driver drop, then reduced by the load line.

RB-C-03.title: Acceleration
RB-C-03.asks: How quickly can the robot speed up?
RB-C-03.note: Driven force minus rolling resistance, over the mass plus the spinning inertia of wheels and gearbox.

RB-C-04.title: Stall current
RB-C-04.asks: If every motor stalls, can the driver and battery supply the current?
RB-C-04.note: Supply voltage over winding resistance for each motor, summed, against the driver, battery and wire ratings.

RB-C-05.title: Logic supply dip
RB-C-05.asks: Does the logic supply stay high enough when the motors start?
RB-C-05.note: Peak motor current times the supply's source resistance against the lowest voltage the logic accepts. This one runs in the circuit solver.

RB-C-06.title: Runtime
RB-C-06.asks: How long does the battery last in this duty profile?
RB-C-06.note: Usable battery energy over mean power, for the stated share of time at cruise, at stall and idle. The answer is a range.

RB-C-07.title: Tipping
RB-C-07.asks: On what slope or braking does the robot tip over?
RB-C-07.note: Angle from the centre of mass to the wheel contacts, sideways and lengthways, against the slope and the acceleration over g.

RB-C-08.title: Arm holding torque
RB-C-08.asks: Can each joint hold the arm and its load still?
RB-C-08.note: Torque of the masses beyond each joint about its axis, against the servo's stall or holding torque.

RB-C-09.title: Encoder resolution
RB-C-09.asks: Is one encoder count small enough to control speed smoothly?
RB-C-09.note: Distance per count from the wheel size, counts per turn and gear ratio, then the speed step per loop period. Above 10 percent of the target speed, control is noisy.

RB-C-10.title: Sensor placement
RB-C-10.asks: Are the sensors at a height and position where they can see?
RB-C-10.note: A line sensor's height and footprint against the line width. A distance sensor's minimum range against the nearest part of the robot in its beam.

problems.RB-E-TREE: The joints must connect the bodies as a tree with exactly one root body. Check {joint}.
problems.RB-E-MASS: {body} has no mass. Give it a mass above 0.
problems.RB-E-INERTIA: The inertia of {body} is not possible: no axis may be larger than the sum of the other two.
problems.RB-E-THIN: {body} has a side of {size_mm} mm. Every collider side must be at least {min_mm} mm.
problems.RB-E-AXIS: The axis of {joint} is zero. Give it a direction.
problems.RB-E-LIMITS: The limits of {joint} are wrong: the lower limit {min} must be below the upper limit {max}. A turn of 360 degrees or more is a continuous joint.
problems.RB-E-DRIVE: {joint} is driven by {component}, which is not a motor, servo or stepper.
problems.RB-E-WHEEL: The wheel {joint} needs a wheel spec and a horizontal axis within 1 degree.
problems.RB-E-SURFACE: {body} refers to the surface {surface}, which does not exist.
problems.RB-E-COUPLING: The motor {component} would be unstable at this step size (step times speed of response is {factor}, above 1). Lower the step or add inertia.
problems.RB-W-TUNNEL: {body} may pass through thin walls: at {speed} m/s it moves {step_mm} mm per step, more than half of {thin_mm} mm.
problems.RB-W-INERTIA-BOX: {body} is a mesh, so its inertia is taken from its bounding box.
problems.RB-W-ASPECT: {body} is {ratio} times longer than it is thick, which makes contact unstable.
problems.RB-W-MASSRATIO: The masses on the two sides of {joint} differ by {ratio} times. The solver may be unstable.
problems.RB-W-CG: The centre of mass is {offset_mm} mm from the middle of the support area, more than half its width of {half_mm} mm. The robot is likely to tip.
problems.RB-W-UNDRIVEN: {joint} has no motor and will move freely. Attach a motor from the parts library.

safety.title: Lab safety
safety.lipo: Charge and store LiPo batteries in a safe place, never leave them charging unattended, and stop using one that is puffy or damaged.
safety.pinch: Wheels, gears and arms can pinch fingers. Keep hands clear when the robot is powered.
safety.stall: A stalled motor gets hot quickly. Cut the power if a motor hums and does not turn.
safety.unattended: Do not leave a powered robot unattended.
safety.simulation: The simulation can show a problem, but it cannot replace care with real hardware.

motor-stall.hint1: Look at the wheel with the power on. Is it held still while the motor is driven?
motor-stall.hint2: Measure the motor current and speed. Is the current high while the speed is near zero?
motor-stall.hint3: The load is more than the motor can turn at this voltage. Reduce the load, add gearing or raise the supply.

motor-direction-reversed.symptom: The robot turns the wrong way
motor-direction-reversed.hint1: Command forward and watch each wheel. Does one of them turn backwards?
motor-direction-reversed.hint2: Check how each motor's two wires reach the driver. Are the left and right motors wired the same way round?
motor-direction-reversed.hint3: One motor is wired backwards. Swap its two wires, or flip its direction in the code.

encoder-channel-swapped.symptom: The encoder counts the wrong way
encoder-channel-swapped.hint1: Turn the wheel forward by hand or in the run and watch the count. Does it go down?
encoder-channel-swapped.hint2: Look at the two encoder channels, A and B, on a scope. Which one leads when the wheel goes forward?
encoder-channel-swapped.hint3: Channels A and B are swapped, so forward counts as backward. Swap the two wires or the two pins in the code.

wheel-slip.symptom: The wheel spins but the robot does not move
wheel-slip.hint1: Watch the wheel and the floor under it. Does the wheel turn while the robot stays put?
wheel-slip.hint2: Compare the wheel speed with the robot's speed over the floor, and look at the weight on the wheel and the floor's grip.
wheel-slip.hint3: The wheel does not grip. Add weight over it, use a grippier tyre or a rougher surface, or accelerate more gently.

driver-undersized.symptom: The motor driver cannot supply enough current
driver-undersized.hint1: Feel or watch the driver chip. Does it overheat or cut out when the motors start?
driver-undersized.hint2: Compare the motor's stall current with the driver's current rating.
driver-undersized.hint3: The driver is rated for less than the motors can draw. Use a stronger driver, a motor that draws less or a lighter load.

battery-sag-reset.symptom: The board resets when the motors start
battery-sag-reset.hint1: Note when the resets happen. Do they come right as the motors switch on?
battery-sag-reset.hint2: Measure the battery or logic supply voltage while the motors start. Does it dip below what the board needs?
battery-sag-reset.hint3: The motors pull the battery voltage down far enough to reset the board. Use a stronger battery, add a capacitor, or power the board from a separate supply.

sensor-too-high.symptom: The line sensor does not see the line
sensor-too-high.hint1: Look at how far the sensor is above the floor. Is it much higher than the sensor's data sheet suggests?
sensor-too-high.hint2: Read the sensor value over the line and over the bare floor. Are the two readings almost the same?
sensor-too-high.hint3: The sensor is too high to tell line from floor. Lower it to the height its data sheet gives.

sensor-saturated.symptom: The line sensor reads the same everywhere
sensor-saturated.hint1: Move the robot over the line and over the floor. Does the sensor value stay at its highest or lowest reading?
sensor-saturated.hint2: Check the light around the sensor and how close it is to the surface. Is it flooded with light or shaded completely?
sensor-saturated.hint3: The sensor is saturated, so it cannot tell dark from light. Shield it from stray light, move it a little higher, or lower the emitter current.

ranger-beam-blocked.symptom: The distance sensor always reads near
ranger-beam-blocked.hint1: Look at what is directly in front of the sensor. Is part of the robot inside its beam?
ranger-beam-blocked.hint2: Compare the distance it reads with the sensor's minimum range and with the distance to the nearest part of the robot.
ranger-beam-blocked.hint3: Part of the robot blocks the beam. Move the sensor so it has a clear view, or move the part.

tip-over.hint1: Watch when it tips: when accelerating, braking, turning or on a slope?
tip-over.hint2: Measure how high the centre of mass is and how far apart the wheels are. Is the robot tall and narrow?
tip-over.hint3: The centre of mass is too high for the wheel spacing. Move heavy parts lower, widen the track, or accelerate and brake more gently.

loop-too-slow.symptom: The speed swings up and down
loop-too-slow.hint1: Plot the speed over time. Does it swing around the target in a steady rhythm?
loop-too-slow.hint2: Open the loop timing panel. Does the control loop take longer than its period, or vary a lot from one pass to the next?
loop-too-slow.hint3: The control loop runs too slowly to keep up. Shorten the work done in each pass, or lower the target rate or the gains.
